question.text: The equation of a circle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>Re</mo><mfenced><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mfenced><mrow><mi>Im</mi><mfenced><mi>z</mi></mfenced></mrow></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>Re</mo><mfenced><mi>z</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>.</mo></math> A line which passes through the centre of the given circle and the vertex of the parabola, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-intercept equal to _________.

solution.text:
We have, Rez2+2Imz2+2Rez=0

where z=x+iy

Equation of circle is x2-y2+2y2+2x=0

x2+y2+2x=0

Centre: -1,0

Parabola : x-32=y-4

Vertex : 3,4

Equation of line ≡y-0=4-03+1x+1

⇒y=x+1

Hence, y-  intercept =1.
